findings.text: The fragment reads 'and the root source of a directed probe angle (acquisition-address or description)'. The word 'root' appears to be a leftover from the store-root clause and reads as a copy artifact; the intended phrase is 'the source of a directed probe angle'. The catalogue slot (probe_angle_source) and its values are correct and the behaviour is unaffected; this is cosmetic in an evidence fragment.

follow_ons: The JT-60SA catalogue jt-60sa.json is the next node: its static description store lives at JT60SA_ROOT/machine_description/{phase}, so it needs a paths.py name (e.g. MACHINE_DESCRIPTION_DIR) resolving to JT60SA_ROOT/machine_description -- outside this node's write scope (declared by the run).

The netcdf static store's read path assumes one file per IDS keyed by the binding's IDS name; a description whose IDSs share a filename with unrelated content would need a per-map naming rule (declared by the run; not needed for JT-60SA's five IDSs).

A read against the netcdf static layout re-opens the same {ids}.nc once per binding of that IDS (no per-file cache); a performance note only, not a correctness defect, and the plan's measure does not call for one.
The fragment's 'root source of a directed probe angle' wording (finding 1).
